mission:
Implement CSV analytics export.
Plan this as a single implementation task for the export (with its tests). Generating and reading the contract is the first step of that task, not a task of its own.
Add src/export.js exporting `exportCsv(records)`, which returns CSV text for analytics records like the ones in src/records.js, with node:test tests in test/export.test.js.
The output must conform to the project export contract. The contract is generated: run `npm run generate-schema` and follow generated/export-contract.json exactly.
Follow docs/CONVENTIONS.md. `npm test` must pass.
hiddenPrerequisite: src/normalize.js (only named inside the packed contract)

planV1.summary: Add `src/export.js` exporting `exportCsv(records)` plus node:test tests in `test/export.test.js`, as one implementation task. The task's first step is to run `npm run generate-schema` and read `generated/export-contract.json`, which is binding. I could not read the contract while planning: `generated/` does not exist in the checkout (it is gitignored), the planner role is read-only so I did not run the generator, and `vendor/export-contract.bundle` is a packed binary. The plan therefore states no CSV format details (columns, order, delimiter, quoting, normalisation, line endings); the worker must take all of them from the generated contract and not from guesses.
assumptions: The contract contents are unknown at planning time: `generated/` is absent, and the only source is the XOR+gzip packed `vendor/export-contract.bundle`, which `scripts/generate-contract.mjs` unpacks. Every format rule is deferred to the worker reading the generated file.
`npm run generate-schema` works with Node built-ins only (the script imports just `node:zlib` and `node:fs`), so no install step is needed.

The contract can be met by the single module `src/export.js`. If it requires another module that does not exist (only `src/records.js` is in `src/`), `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` forbids writing it inside this task: it has to be added to the plan as its own task with its own tests, and this task waits for it.

`generated/` stays uncommitted (`.gitignore` lists it and `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` says it is never committed), so the tests must not depend on that directory existing unless the contract itself says so.
`npm test` is `node --test`, which auto-discovers `test/export.test.js` alongside the existing `test/records.test.js`; no `package.json` change is needed.
Invalid input to `exportCsv` throws `TypeError`, per `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`; what counts as invalid is defined by the contract where it speaks to it.
acceptanceCriteria: `src/export.js` exists as plain ESM with no dependencies and exports a function `exportCsv(records)` that returns a CSV string.
The output of `exportCsv` for the records in `src/records.js` (`SAMPLE`) conforms to every rule in `generated/export-contract.json` as produced by `npm run generate-schema`.
`test/export.test.js` uses node:test and asserts the contract's rules against concrete expected output, including a bad-input case that expects `TypeError`.
`npm test` exits 0, with both `test/records.test.js` and `test/export.test.js` passing.

`git status` shows only `src/export.js` and `test/export.test.js` as new files; `generated/` is not committed, and `vendor/export-contract.bundle`, `scripts/generate-contract.mjs` and `package.json` are unmodified.

tasks.title: Implement exportCsv in src/export.js with node:test tests, following the generated export contract
tasks.description:
Repository: analytics-kit, plain ESM JavaScript (`"type": "module"` in package.json), no dependencies, tests with node:test under `test/`, run with `npm test` (`node --test`). Platform is native Windows 11; use PowerShell-compatible commands.

Step 1 (mandatory, before writing any code): run `npm run generate-schema`. This runs `scripts/generate-contract.mjs`, which unpacks `vendor/export-contract.bundle` into `generated/export-contract.json`. Read that JSON file in full. It is the binding export contract and was NOT readable at planning time, so this description deliberately gives no format details. Take every rule from the contract: columns and their order, header row, delimiter, quoting and escaping, line endings and trailing newline, row ordering, and any per-field normalisation (for example whitespace, Unicode, number, currency-case or timestamp handling). Follow it exactly; do not guess or fall back on generic CSV defaults where the contract is specific. If the contract is ambiguous or contradicts this description, the contract wins for format questions; report the ambiguity rather than silently choosing.

Step 2: read `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` and `src/records.js`. `src/records.js` exports `SAMPLE`, two analytics records with fields `id`, `customer`, `amount`, `currency`, `timestamp`. The sample is intentionally messy: a customer with leading/trailing and repeated inner spaces, a customer containing a combining accent (`e` + U+0301), an amount given as the string '12.5' and another as the number 3, currency in lower and upper case, a timestamp with a +02:00 offset and one in Z, and ids out of order (r2 before r1). Expect the contract to say how each of these is handled.

Step 3: create `src/export.js` exporting `exportCsv(records)`, which returns the CSV text for an array of such records per the contract. Use only Node built-ins. Errors thrown for bad input must be `TypeError` (conventions). Do not mutate the input records. Match the style of the existing code (no semicolons, single quotes, brief comments).

Step 4: create `test/export.test.js` using `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, in the style of `test/records.test.js`. Cover: the exact expected CSV string for `SAMPLE` derived by hand from the contract (not by copying the implementation's output), each distinct contract rule with a focused case (including quoting/escaping of fields that contain the delimiter, quotes or newlines if the contract defines it), the empty-array case as the contract defines it, and bad input throwing `TypeError`. Tests must not require `generated/` to exist unless the contract says to read it at runtime, because `generated/` is gitignored and never committed.

Step 5: run `npm test` and make it pass without weakening or skipping any test.

Scope constraints from `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`: this task creates only `src/export.js` and `test/export.test.js`. If the contract turns out to require a module that does not exist in the repo (for example a shared helper it names by path), do NOT write it inside this task: stop, report it via the blocker/plan-change mechanism so it is added to the plan as its own task with its own tests, and wait for it. Do not edit `vendor/export-contract.bundle`, `scripts/generate-contract.mjs`, `src/records.js` or `package.json`, and do not commit `generated/`. Remove any temporary files or scripts you create.

In your result, list the contract rules you read and which test covers each.
acceptanceCriteria: `npm run generate-schema` was run and `generated/export-contract.json` exists locally; the task result lists the contract rules that were read.
`src/export.js` is dependency-free ESM and exports `exportCsv(records)` returning a string.
`exportCsv(SAMPLE)` (from `src/records.js`) equals the exact CSV string the contract prescribes, verified by a test whose expected value is written out literally.
Every rule in `generated/export-contract.json` that affects output is covered by at least one assertion in `test/export.test.js`.
Bad input (as defined by the contract and conventions) throws `TypeError`, and a test asserts it.
`npm test` exits 0 with `test/records.test.js` and `test/export.test.js` both passing, with no skipped tests.
Only `src/export.js` and `test/export.test.js` are added; no other tracked file is modified and `generated/` is not staged or committed.
If the contract requires a module not delivered by this task, the task reports that as a blocker/plan change instead of creating the module.

risks.description: The contract was not readable at planning time (generated/ absent, bundle is packed binary, planner is read-only), so the scope and complexity of the task are estimated without knowing the actual rules.
risks.mitigation: The task makes generating and reading the contract its mandatory first step, defers every format decision to it, and requires the worker to list the rules read and map each to a test.

risks.description: The contract may require a module that no task in this plan delivers; docs/CONVENTIONS.md forbids writing such a module inside the export task.
risks.mitigation: The task description tells the worker to stop and raise a blocker/plan change so the module is added as its own task with tests, and to wait for it rather than create it inline.

risks.description: The worker may fall back on generic CSV habits (RFC 4180 quoting, CRLF, input order) where the contract says something different, especially for the messy SAMPLE values (whitespace, combining accent, mixed amount types, currency case, timezone offsets, id order).
risks.mitigation: The description calls out each of these sample quirks and requires expected values in tests to be derived by hand from the contract, not from the implementation's output.

risks.description: Tests could depend on generated/export-contract.json, which is gitignored and absent on a clean checkout, making `npm test` fail elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: The task requires tests not to depend on generated/ unless the contract explicitly demands it, and an acceptance criterion checks generated/ is not committed.

risks.description: `npm run generate-schema` could fail (corrupt bundle or Node version mismatch), leaving no contract to follow.
risks.mitigation: The worker reports a blocker with the command output instead of guessing the format; the bundle and generator script must not be edited.
